facts.fact: AWS announced Amazon Bedrock AgentCore GA in October 2025 in nine Regions, with VPC support, 8-hour execution windows and session isolation (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-available/)
AgentCore has supported the A2A protocol since its GA in October 2025 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-available/)
AgentCore Gateway turns APIs and Lambda functions into MCP tools (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-available/)

As of 2026-11 the AgentCore devguide lists 13 modular services: Harness, Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability, Payments, Evaluations, Optimization, Policy and Registry, which work alone or together with any model (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/what-is-bedrock-agentcore.html)

AgentCore services work with any framework, including CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Strands Agents, Google ADK and OpenAI Agents SDK (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/what-is-bedrock-agentcore.html)

The AgentCore harness (managed agent loop) has been GA since June 2026, with the What's New post dated 2026-06-17, after public preview started in April 2026 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/06/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-harness-generally-available)

With the AgentCore harness you define a model, system prompt and tools in one config (`CreateHarness`) and call `InvokeHarness`; each session runs in an isolated microVM with filesystem and shell (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/06/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-harness-generally-available)
Since November 2026 the AgentCore harness defaults use Strands with Claude Opus 5 in commercial Regions (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)
The harness is one of the AgentCore modular services, providing a managed agent loop (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/06/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-harness-generally-available)

AgentCore Runtime hosts agents or MCP servers in containers or direct code (serverless microVMs) and supports HTTP (port 8080 `/invocations`, `/ws`), MCP (port 8000 `/mcp`), A2A (port 9000 `/`) and AG-UI, with SigV4 or OAuth 2.0 inbound auth (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-service-contract.html)
AgentCore Runtime supports the AG-UI protocol alongside HTTP, MCP and A2A (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-service-contract.html)

An AgentCore Runtime "Instances" compute type with capacity providers was added in August 2026 and runs on EC2 in your account (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)
Instances is an AgentCore Runtime compute type added in August 2026 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

AgentCore Memory provides short-term and long-term memory, with episodic memory added in December 2025, TTL on long-term records in October 2026, and direct `IngestData` in August 2026 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/12/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-policy-evaluations-preview/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)
AgentCore short-term memory moved to consumption-based pricing in October 2026 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

AgentCore Identity is the agent identity and credential vault: it provides workload identities, OAuth2 and API-key credential providers for outbound calls, and token vault storage (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/what-is-bedrock-agentcore.html)
AgentCore Identity works with Cognito, Okta, Entra ID and Auth0 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/what-is-bedrock-agentcore.html)

AgentCore Identity additions include OBO token exchange (April 2026), Private Key JWT client auth (July 2026) and a Consent Portal (September 2026) (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

Policy in AgentCore has been GA since March 2026; policies sit in a policy engine attached to an AgentCore Gateway and are evaluated on every tool call (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/)
You author AgentCore policies in natural language that converts to Cedar (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/)
The AgentCore devguide now names the policy language Dogwood, which is Cedar-compatible (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/what-is-bedrock-agentcore.html)

Bedrock Guardrails support was added to Policy in AgentCore in June 2026 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/what-is-bedrock-agentcore.html)
AgentCore Evaluations has been GA since 2026-03-31, in nine Regions at GA (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/agentcore-evaluations-generally-available/)

AgentCore Evaluations offers online evaluation of sampled production traces and on-demand evaluation for CI/CD, with 13 built-in evaluators plus custom LLM-judge or Lambda evaluators; Batch Evaluations and A/B Testing went GA in June 2026, and Failure Insights entered preview in June 2026 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/agentcore-evaluations-generally-available/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

AgentCore Optimization (Recommendations, configuration bundles, A/B testing) has been GA since June 2026 after public preview from April 2026 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

AgentCore Optimization optimizes system prompts and tool descriptions from traces, using A/B traffic splitting through Gateway (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

AgentCore Observability emits OTEL-compatible telemetry to CloudWatch, and cross-account monitoring was added in April 2026 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)
AgentCore Observability telemetry is OTEL-compatible (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

Since 2026-07-20, new AgentCore agents write spans to their own log group by default, while older agents keep `aws/spans` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

AWS Agent Registry is a governed catalog of MCP servers, agents, skills and tools, with approval workflows, hybrid search and a native MCP endpoint (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)
AWS Agent Registry reached AWS GovCloud (US-West) on 2026-11-06 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/aws-agent-registry-govcloud-us-west/)

AWS recommends migrating from Bedrock Agents Classic to the AgentCore harness, or to code-defined agents on AgentCore Runtime (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-classic-maintenance-mode.html)
A migration skill for Bedrock Agents Classic is in the Agent Toolkit for AWS (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-classic-maintenance-mode.html)

Bedrock Guardrails are not affected by Agents Classic maintenance mode: guardrails set on the model still apply, and agent-level enforcement in AgentCore goes through Gateway policies (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-classic-maintenance-mode.html)
Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base (fully managed RAG) has been GA since June 2026 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/06/amazon-bedrock-managed-knowledge-base/)

Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base manages vector storage and offers hybrid search, reranking and agentic multi-hop retrieval, with six native connectors: S3, SharePoint, Confluence, Google Drive, OneDrive and Web Crawler (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/06/amazon-bedrock-managed-knowledge-base/)
Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base integrates natively with AgentCore (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/06/amazon-bedrock-managed-knowledge-base/)

Bedrock Guardrails cross-account safeguards have been GA since April 2026: you enforce guardrails across an AWS Organization from the management account, at organization, account or application level (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/04/bedrock-guardrails-cross-account-safeguards/)

The Bedrock model catalog is serverless, and models are enabled by default (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/simplified-amazon-bedrock-model-access/)

facts.fact: Anthropic models before Claude Opus 4.7 still need a one-time first-time-use form (`PutUseCaseForModelAccess`), filed once per account or org; starting with Claude Opus 4.7 it is not needed, and it never applies through `bedrock-mantle` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access.html)
Claude Opus 4.7 on Bedrock doesn't need the Anthropic first-time-use form (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access.html)

Amazon SageMaker AI covers custom model training, fine-tuning and hosting; serverless model customization (SFT, DPO, RFT, LoRA, full fine-tuning) launched in December 2025 and expanded through October 2026, and training session APIs launched in October 2026 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/12/new-serverless-model-customization-capability-amazon-sagemaker-ai/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/10/training-session-apis-on-sagemaker-ai/)

SageMaker AI serverless model customization and training session APIs run in us-east-1, us-west-2, ap-northeast-1 and eu-west-1, with training sessions also in ap-south-1 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/10/training-session-apis-on-sagemaker-ai/)

Lambda durable functions bring checkpointed multi-step workflows into Lambda with `steps` and `waits`, suspend for up to one year without compute charges, and support Python 3.13/3.14 and Node.js 22/24 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/12/lambda-durable-multi-step-applications-ai-workflows/)
Lambda durable functions launched in December 2025, initially GA in us-east-2 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/12/lambda-durable-multi-step-applications-ai-workflows/)

Step Functions has an optimized integration for the AgentCore harness with resource `arn:aws:states:::bedrockagentcore:invokeHarness` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/connect-bedrockagentcore.html)

The Step Functions AgentCore harness integration is request-response only (no `.sync` or `.waitForTaskToken`) and returns only the final assistant text in Converse shape; the Task state is capped at 900 s even if `TimeoutSeconds` is higher, and the harness keeps running after the Task times out (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/connect-bedrockagentcore.html)

AWS Quick (formerly Amazon Quick and Amazon Quick Suite, formerly QuickSight) is the business-user agent workspace, offering chat agents, autonomous and always-on agents, flows, apps and deep research (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/amazon-quick-aws-quick/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/09/amazon-quick-always-on-agents-sharper-feed-enterprise-controls/)

facts.fact: Amazon Q Developer CLI and IDE became Kiro, and the Q Developer console became the Kiro console (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/upgrade-to-kiro.html)
In November 2026, Q Developer in the AWS Console was renamed "AWS assistant" (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/q-developer-renamed-aws-assistant/)
AWS MCP Server, AWS's managed remote MCP server, has been GA since 2026-05-06; its preview was announced at re:Invent 2025 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/05/aws-mcp-server/)
AWS MCP Server is part of the Agent Toolkit for AWS (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/05/aws-mcp-server/)

One AWS MCP Server endpoint lets an agent call any AWS API, run sandboxed Python, search and read docs, and load agent skills, with IAM guardrails, CloudWatch metrics and CloudTrail logging, at no additional charge (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/05/aws-mcp-server/)
AWS MCP Server endpoints follow the pattern `https://aws-mcp.<region>.api.aws/mcp` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)

The AWS MCP Server setup guide lists us-east-1, us-west-2, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-northeast-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1 and eu-west-2, newer than the May 2026 GA post, which listed only us-east-1 and eu-central-1 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)

AWS MCP Server has about a dozen tools in two groups: no-credential tools (search and read documentation, list Regions, regional availability) and IAM-authenticated tools (`aws___call_aws` for any API, run script in a sandbox, retrieve skill, get tasks, S3 presigned URL) (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/how-amazon-cloudfront-secures-and-accelerates-the-aws-mcp-server/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/understanding-iam-for-managed-aws-mcp-servers/)

AWS MCP Server auth option A is OAuth 2.1 through AWS Sign-in with no local proxy; access tokens last 1 hour and auto-refresh for up to 12 hours, and multi-profile switching is not supported (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)

For AWS MCP Server OAuth, the principal needs the managed policy `AWSMCPSignInOAuthAccessPolicy` (`signin:AuthorizeOAuth2Access`, `signin:CreateOAuth2Token`) (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)

Some clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Kiro IDE) need `?oauth=initialize` appended to the AWS MCP Server URL (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)

`aws signin create-oauth2-token-with-iam --grant-type client_credentials` is the headless client-credentials path for AWS MCP Server OAuth: it signs with SigV4 and returns a Bearer token that lasts 3600 s (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/introducing-oauth-support-for-aws-mcp-server/)
The AWS MCP Server OAuth support announcement is dated 2026-07-09 (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/introducing-oauth-support-for-aws-mcp-server/)

AWS MCP Server auth option B is SigV4 through the MCP Proxy for AWS: run `uvx mcp-proxy-for-aws-cli@latest https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp --metadata AWS_REGION=us-west-2`, which needs AWS CLI ≥ 2.32.0 and uv; this option supports read-only mode, multiple profiles and a default Region (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)

Claude Code adds AWS MCP Server for OAuth with `claude mcp add aws-mcp https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp --transport http` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)

MCP Proxy for AWS (`mcp-proxy-for-aws`, PyPI) is GA, open source and at version 1.8.0 (2026-11-03); GA was announced in October 2025 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/model-context-protocol-proxy-available/ ; https://pypi.org/pypi/mcp-proxy-for-aws/json)

MCP Proxy for AWS SigV4-signs MCP traffic to AWS-hosted MCP servers and to AgentCore Gateway or Runtime endpoints, and has read-only mode and retries (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/model-context-protocol-proxy-available/)

IAM context keys `aws:ViaAWSMCPService` (bool) and `aws:CalledViaAWSMCP` (string, for example `aws-mcp.amazonaws.com`, `eks-mcp.amazonaws.com`, `ecs-mcp.amazonaws.com`) cover all AWS-managed MCP servers and can be used in IAM policies or SCPs to deny or limit actions an agent takes through MCP, for example to deny S3 deletes through MCP (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/understanding-iam-for-managed-aws-mcp-servers/)

The boolean IAM context key `aws:ViaAWSMCPService` is set on calls made through AWS-managed MCP servers such as AWS MCP Server (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/understanding-iam-for-managed-aws-mcp-servers/)
AWS Knowledge MCP Server (remote, no AWS account, rate-limited) has been GA since October 2025 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/aws-knowledge-mcp-server-generally-available/)

AWS Knowledge MCP Server's endpoint is `https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws` with no auth, and its tools are `search_documentation`, `read_documentation`, `recommend`, `list_regions` and `get_regional_availability` (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/aws-knowledge-mcp-server-generally-available/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/infrastructure-and-automation/accelerate-region-expansion-with-the-aws-knowledge-mcp-server/)

AWS now recommends the AWS MCP Server instead of the AWS Knowledge MCP Server (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/infrastructure-and-automation/accelerate-region-expansion-with-the-aws-knowledge-mcp-server/)

The AWS setup guide says to remove `aws-api-mcp-server` and `aws-knowledge-mcp-server` when you adopt AWS MCP Server, because overlapping tools confuse agents (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)

AWS API MCP Server (local, open source, container in ECR Public) reached v1.0.0 in October 2025, adding streamable HTTP, elicitation, a deny-list and consent for mutating actions, and `get_execution_plan` (experimental) (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/aws-api-mcp-server-v1-0-0-release/)

AgentCore Gateway aggregates MCP targets into a single virtual MCP server with one `tools/list`; target types are Lambda functions, API Gateway REST API stages, OpenAPI schemas, Smithy models, remote MCP servers, built-in integration templates and built-in connectors (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-targets-mcp.html)
AgentCore Gateway offers semantic tool search and target-level 3LO OAuth, which went GA in April 2026 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-targets-mcp.html)

Since June 2026 AgentCore Gateway has HTTP passthrough targets and inference targets that route LLM traffic to providers through model-based routing, and AgentCore Runtime targets went GA in June 2026 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-supported-targets.html)

October 2026 added a Step Functions connector, MCP Tasks, model fallback and private CA for targets to AgentCore Gateway (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

AgentCore Gateway built-in integration templates cover 16 providers: Amazon, Asana, BambooHR, Brave, Coinbase x402 Bazaar, Confluence, Jira, Microsoft, PagerDuty, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Slack, Smartsheet, Tavily, Zendesk and Zoom (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-target-integrations.html)
The AgentCore Gateway built-in Web Search Tool connector went GA in June 2026 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)
The AgentCore Gateway built-in Web Answer connector went GA in November 2026 in us-east-1 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

AgentCore Gateway inbound auth options are JWT (`CUSTOM_JWT` with `discoveryUrl`, `allowedAudience`, `allowedClients`, `allowedScopes` and `customClaims`), IAM (`AWS_IAM`, which needs `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway`) or offloaded ("Authenticate only" and `NONE`) (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-inbound-auth.html)

The AgentCore CLI defaults gateway inbound auth to `NONE` (unauthenticated) if you omit `--authorizer-type` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-using-auth-ex-starter.html)
AgentCore Gateway outbound auth to targets uses the IAM role, API keys or OAuth through AgentCore Identity (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-inbound-auth.html)

The AgentCore Gateway URL pattern is `https://{gateway-Id}.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.{Region}.amazonaws.com`, the control plane is `bedrock-agentcore-control.<region>.amazonaws.com`, and the service principal is `bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/bedrock-agentcore-limits.html)

`bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com` is the recommended Bedrock inference endpoint and serves InvokeModel, Converse, OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses (at `/openai/v1`), and the Anthropic Messages API (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html)

`bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws` serves Responses, Chat Completions and Messages; both Bedrock endpoints run on the same Mantle engine at the same per-token price (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html)
`bedrock-runtime` serves the OpenAI-compatible Responses and Chat Completions APIs at `/openai/v1` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html)
`bedrock-runtime` serves the Anthropic Messages API, and `bedrock-mantle` serves Messages too (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html)

Only `bedrock-runtime` supports Guardrails, intelligent prompt routing, custom inference profiles, batch and Provisioned Throughput (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html)

Only `bedrock-mantle` supports server-side tools (such as web search), background inference (`background=true`), Projects and Workspaces (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html)
Mantle inference IAM uses `bedrock-mantle:CreateInference` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/scaling-throughput-best-practices.html)

facts.fact: Bedrock API keys (bearer tokens) work with the OpenAI SDK: set `OPENAI_BASE_URL` to the Bedrock base URL and `OPENAI_API_KEY` to the Bedrock key (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-responses-api.html)

Short-term Bedrock API keys last up to 12 hours, inherit the caller's IAM permissions and are recommended by AWS; long-term keys create an IAM user with `AmazonBedrockLimitedAccess` and are meant for exploration only (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.html)
A long-term Bedrock API key creates an IAM user with `AmazonBedrockLimitedAccess` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.html)
boto3, the Python package for AWS calls, is at version 1.44.3 (https://pypi.org/pypi/bedrock-agentcore/json)
Strands Agents, the open-source agent framework, is at version 1.65.0 (https://pypi.org/pypi/bedrock-agentcore/json)

`bedrock-agentcore`, the AgentCore runtime SDK for Python (`BedrockAgentCoreApp`), is at version 1.26.0 (2026-11-10) (https://pypi.org/pypi/bedrock-agentcore/json ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/agentcore-python-sdk-reference.html)

There is also an AgentCore client in the AWS SDK for Python v4 docs, installed with `pip install aws-sdk-bedrock-agentcore` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-python/v4/reference/clients/bedrock-agentcore/)
JS/TS agent work on AWS uses the `@aws-sdk/*` v3 clients (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/agentcore-python-sdk-reference.html)

A2A and AG-UI are supported agent protocols on AgentCore Runtime; the `ProtocolConfiguration.serverProtocol` values are `MCP | HTTP | A2A | AGUI` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore-control/latest/APIReference/API_ProtocolConfiguration.html)
AgentCore Runtime accepts `AGUI` as a `ProtocolConfiguration.serverProtocol` value (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore-control/latest/APIReference/API_ProtocolConfiguration.html)
The AgentCore Runtime protocol port is configurable from 8000 to 12000, except 8443 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore-control/latest/APIReference/API_ProtocolConfiguration.html)

AWS Quick is an MCP client for external MCP servers, supporting SSE and streamable HTTP with 3LO, 2LO or no auth, and discovers OAuth through RFC 9728 and Dynamic Client Registration (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/mcp-integration.html)
Since August 2026 AWS Quick can enable MCP servers and agents from AWS Agent Registry (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/aws-agent-registry-agents-mcp-servers-quick/)

AWS Quick has built-in action connectors to SaaS; thirteen were added in April 2026, including Google Workspace apps, Zoom, QuickBooks, Airtable and Dropbox, alongside the earlier Salesforce, Jira, ServiceNow and Microsoft 365 connectors (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/04/amazon-quick-google-workspace-zoom/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/09/amazon-quick-custom-apps-natural-language/)

The common event-driven agent pattern is EventBridge (rules or Scheduler) to Lambda to `InvokeAgentRuntime`; AWS samples trigger AgentCore Runtime agents from schedules and webhooks this way (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/building-a-context-aware-ai-assistant-on-agentcore-and-openclaw/)

In the event-driven agent pattern, a Lambda function calls `InvokeAgentRuntime` to run an AgentCore Runtime agent (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/building-a-context-aware-ai-assistant-on-agentcore-and-openclaw/)

PrivateLink interface endpoints for Bedrock use the suffixes `bedrock`, `bedrock-runtime`, `bedrock-mantle`, `bedrock-agent` and `bedrock-agent-runtime`, each as `com.amazonaws.<region>.<suffix>` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html)

PrivateLink has three interface endpoints for AgentCore: `com.amazonaws.<region>.bedrock-agentcore` (data plane), `com.amazonaws.<region>.bedrock-agentcore-control` and `com.amazonaws.<region>.bedrock-agentcore.gateway` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html)
AgentCore VPC endpoint policies can only filter IAM principals, so OAuth callers need `Principal: *` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html)

JDBC and ODBC drivers don't apply to the in-scope AWS agent services (IAM, Bedrock, AgentCore, Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge), which are reached through HTTPS APIs and SDKs; database drivers belong to separate database services (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html)

On Windows, install AWS CLI v2 with the signed PowerShell script `irm https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/install.ps1 | iex` (recommended; per user to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Amazon\AWSCLIV2`, `-System` for all users) or the MSIs `msiexec.exe /i https://awscli.amazonaws.com/AWSCLIV2.msi` (all users) and `AWSCLIV2-User.msi` (current user) (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html)

facts.fact: `aws login` signs the CLI in with console credentials and is the recommended local-dev method; it works for root, IAM users and federated identities, `--remote` handles devices without a browser, and credentials auto-refresh every 15 minutes for up to the principal's session limit (max 12 h) (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-sign-in.html)

The `aws login` cache is `%USERPROFILE%\.aws\login\cache` (override with `AWS_LOGIN_CACHE_DIRECTORY`), the profile gets `login_session = <arn>`, and `aws logout [--all]` signs out (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-sign-in.html)

You can restrict `aws login` with IAM by targeting `arn:aws:signin:region:account-id:oauth2/public-client/localhost` (same device) and `.../remote` (cross-device); for SDKs that don't support login credentials yet, serve them through `credential_process` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-sign-in.html)

`aws configure sso` and `aws configure sso-session` set up IAM Identity Center sign-in by writing an `[sso-session]` section with `sso_start_url`, `sso_region` and `sso_registration_scopes = sso:account:access`, plus a profile with `sso_account_id` and `sso_role_name` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-sso.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-files.html)
After configuring SSO you run `aws sso login [--profile X | --sso-session Y]`, and tokens are cached in `~/.aws/sso/cache` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-sso.html)

PKCE has been the default `aws sso login` flow since CLI 2.22.0 and must complete on the same device; use `--use-device-code` for headless devices (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-sso.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/developer/aws-cli-adds-pkce-based-authorization-for-sso/)

The AgentCore CLI is installed with `npm install -g @aws/agentcore` and is at v1.0.3 (Node ≥ 20.12.0); v1.0 shipped in October 2026, after GA as v0.4.0 in March 2026 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/agentcore-get-started-cli.html ; https://registry.npmjs.org/@aws/agentcore/latest ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

Key AgentCore CLI commands are `agentcore create`, `add gateway`, `add gateway-target`, `add credentials`, `deploy`, `invoke`, `migrate` (v0 projects) and `update` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/agentcore-get-started-cli.html)

On Windows, the old pip `agentcore` command can shadow the npm one; if `agentcore --version` errors, run `pip uninstall bedrock-agentcore-starter-toolkit` and open a new terminal (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/agentcore-get-started-cli.html)
Kiro CLI (`kiro-cli`, formerly Amazon Q Developer CLI) is AWS's agentic coding CLI (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/upgrade-to-kiro.html)

Kiro CLI version 2.11 and later can add AWS MCP Server natively with `kiro-cli mcp add --name aws-mcp --url https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)
The Agent Toolkit for AWS ships agent skills installed with `npx skills add aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws/skills` (https://aws.amazon.com/products/developer-tools/agent-toolkit-for-aws/)
AWS recommends pinning the MCP proxy version, for example `mcp-proxy-for-aws@1.6.3`, for reproducible behavior (https://aws.amazon.com/products/developer-tools/agent-toolkit-for-aws/)

The Agent Toolkit for AWS docs (AWS MCP Server setup, quotas, OAuth) are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/ (verified 200), and the repo is https://github.com/aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/getting-started-aws-mcp-server.html)
awslabs MCP docs are at https://awslabs.github.io/mcp/ (verified 200), with source at https://github.com/awslabs/mcp (https://awslabs.github.io/mcp/)
AWS Knowledge MCP is a docs MCP server at `https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws` (verified 200) (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/aws-knowledge-mcp-server-generally-available/)
The documentation tools in AWS MCP Server need no credentials (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/aws-knowledge-mcp-server-generally-available/)

For AWS release notes, status and samples use What's New at https://aws.amazon.com/new/ and the AWS Health Dashboard status page at https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status (both verified 200), plus the sample repos https://github.com/awslabs/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-samples and https://github.com/aws/agentcore-cli (https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status ; https://github.com/awslabs/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-samples)

Bedrock `bedrock-runtime` throttling is per model and per Region (TPM, sometimes also RPM), and all APIs share the quota: InvokeModel, Converse, Responses and Chat Completions, even though quota names say "InvokeModel" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-runtime.html)
`bedrock-mantle` quotas are counted separately from `bedrock-runtime`, with separate input and output TPM and no RPM (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html)

Bedrock output tokens burn down quota faster than input tokens: for recent Claude models each output token counts as 5, and quota use = input + cache-write input + output × burndown rate (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/global-cross-region-inference-for-latest-anthropic-claude-opus-sonnet-and-haiku-models-on-amazon-bedrock-in-thailand-malaysia-singapore-indonesia-and-taiwan/)

An unset `max_tokens` is a top cause of agent throttling: Bedrock reserves input + `max_tokens` at admission, and if `max_tokens` is unset it reserves the model maximum (for example 64,000 for Claude Sonnet); the unused part is returned after completion (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/optimize-your-applications-for-scale-and-reliability-on-amazon-bedrock/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html)

Cross-Region inference (CRIS) profiles raise throughput, and each profile type has its own quota pool; geographic profiles use prefixes such as `us.` and `eu.`, global profiles use `global.`, and quotas such as "Global cross-Region model inference tokens per minute for ${Model}" are viewed and raised in the source Region (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/global-cross-region-inference.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/access-openai-gpt-models-on-amazon-bedrock-from-canada-with-cross-region-inference/)

Cross-Region inference fails with `AccessDeniedException` when SCPs block destination Regions: geographic CRIS needs every destination Region allowed, global CRIS needs `aws:RequestedRegion` = `unspecified` and the Region-agnostic ARN `arn:aws:bedrock:::foundation-model/...`, or you can exempt with the `bedrock:InferenceProfileArn` condition key (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html ; https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-access-denied-exception)

On `bedrock-runtime`, the Responses API rejects `background=true` (400) and application inference profiles (400) and has no server-side tools; stored responses belong to the Region that served them (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html)

A wrong `bedrock-mantle` path prefix makes requests fail: some models are served under `/v1` and others under `/openai/v1`, and a wrong prefix returns "model ... isn't supported on this route" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-responses-api.html)
Listing models against the `bedrock-runtime` `/openai/v1` URL returns `404 UnknownOperationException` (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-chat-completions.html)

facts.fact: AgentCore Runtime session limits: synchronous request timeout 15 min, async jobs up to 8 h on microVMs (14 days on Instances), payloads capped at 100 MB, streaming connections up to 60 min, idle timeout default 15 min (`idleRuntimeSessionTimeout`), max session lifetime default 8 h (`maxLifetime`), and 1 GB session storage (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/bedrock-agentcore-limits.html)

AgentCore Runtime throttles at 1,000 TPS for data-plane calls and 25 TPS for new sessions, both adjustable and shared per account, simplified in August 2026 from 200 TPS and per-endpoint limits; control-plane mutations are 50 TPS (not adjustable), active sessions are 5,000 in us-east-1 and us-west-2 and 2,500 in other Regions, and cross-account calls count against the owner's quota (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/bedrock-agentcore-limits.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html)

AgentCore Runtime images are capped at 2 GB on platform V1 and 10 GB on V2; direct-code zips are 250 MB compressed and 750 MB uncompressed; environment variables are 4 KB per agent; sessions get 2 vCPU/8 GB by default, up to 8 vCPU/32 GB with resource configurations on V2 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/bedrock-agentcore-limits.html)

AgentCore Gateway limits (all adjustable): 100 targets per gateway, 1,000 tools per target, 15 min invocation timeout, 6 MB tool payloads, tool-call and tool-list rates of 200 TPS per gateway and per account, 5,000 concurrent connections, 25 search-based tool calls per minute, and 10 TPS each for Web Search and Web Answer (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/bedrock-agentcore-limits.html)

AgentCore Memory limits: 150 resources per Region, 200 `CreateEvent` per second per account, 5 per second per actor and session, and 150,000 TPM for long-term extraction (adjustable) (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/bedrock-agentcore-limits.html)
AgentCore Browser allows 1,000 concurrent sessions, each with 1 vCPU/4 GB (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/bedrock-agentcore-limits.html)
AgentCore Code Interpreter allows 1,000 concurrent sessions, each with 2 vCPU/8 GB (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/bedrock-agentcore-limits.html)

AgentCore Policy has a 400 KB Cedar schema cap per policy engine that grows with tool count and parameter complexity across all attached gateways, so split engines if you hit it; Policy APIs run at 1 to 5 TPS (not adjustable) (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/bedrock-agentcore-limits.html)

A Gateway-to-Runtime auth mismatch fails with "Authorization method mismatch": an IAM runtime needs an IAM (SigV4) or Caller-IAM target, and a JWT runtime needs an OAuth or token-passthrough target (https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-resolve-authorization-method)

AWS MCP Server rate limits are not adjustable: authenticated requests get 10 per second sustained per account per Region, unauthenticated requests get 5 per second per source IP and only the read-only knowledge tools, and throttled requests return 429 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/aws-mcp-limits.html)

Lambda limits for agent tools: timeout 900 s (90 min for Managed Instances async and ESM invocations); synchronous payloads 6 MB each way, async payloads 1 MB, streamed responses up to 200 MB at 2 MBps after the first 6 MB; default concurrency 1,000 per Region, with new accounts starting lower (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html)

STS `AssumeRole` `DurationSeconds` goes up to 43,200 s (12 h), subject to the role's max session setting, but role chaining caps sessions at 1 hour and any value above 3,600 s fails when chaining (https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/iam-role-chaining-limit)
